lessons.title: Who does what?
lessons.body: A2A lets independently built agents communicate and coordinate work. MCP connects an agent to tools and resources. A marketplace helps buyers find offers; it is a sales channel, not the A2A protocol. AP2 addresses evidence of purchase and payment authority. A payment processor handles the money. A chat message saying ‘approved’ is not a verified payment mandate.

lessons.title: Discover a service and agree on the work
lessons.body: An Agent Card describes an agent’s identity, skills, connection details and supported capabilities. It can be found through a known address, a registry or direct configuration. A useful description is not proof that a seller is trustworthy. For this exercise, agree the deliverable, inputs, price, deadline and acceptance criteria separately. Publishing a card does not guarantee customers.

lessons.title: Give authority before autonomous purchasing
lessons.body: Human-not-present purchasing starts with authority the user has already granted. AP2 v0.2 distinguishes Checkout Mandates from Payment Mandates, with open constraints and closed authorization for a specific transaction. The checkout and payment must be bound together and verified. A low price does not excuse missing authority or a changed subscription term. This lab’s spending limits are fictional business rules, not limits imposed by the protocol.

lessons.title: Verify, pay and retain evidence
lessons.body: A trusted approval surface obtains the user’s consent. Verifiers check the evidence; the model’s confidence is not the verification mechanism. Separate discovery, authority, payment outcome and delivery acceptance in the record. A timeout alone does not tell you whether a payment succeeded. In our exercise, an unknown outcome calls for checking the existing transaction before trying again.

lessons.title: Track the result and the business
lessons.body: An A2A interaction can return a message or a task. A task can request input or authorization, complete, fail, be rejected or be canceled. A completed task is not by itself proof that money settled or that the buyer accepted the work. A later revision of a terminal task starts new work rather than reopening it. Our buyer also keeps the agreed scope, receipts and accepted version, and checks delivery cost and margin.

quiz.question: Which part connects one independent agent to another?
options: A2A
A payment processor
A marketplace listing
quiz.why: A2A is the agent communication layer. A listing helps discovery; a processor moves money.

quiz.question: A seller has an Agent Card. What have you established?
options: Its claims and connection details are available
It is trustworthy and every purchase is authorized
It has a guaranteed stream of buyers
quiz.why: A card describes capabilities. Identity, trust, commercial terms and purchasing authority still need checking.

quiz.question: An agent finds a $40 offer below a $50 limit, but no valid purchase or payment authority exists. What next?
options: Pay because the price is low
Obtain and verify the required authority
Ask the seller to call it free and charge later
quiz.why: Price compliance is only one condition. The agent cannot infer authority from a budget number.

quiz.question: Authority covers a one-time purchase. The seller switches to $10 per month. What next?
options: Proceed because this month is cheaper
Accept twelve months automatically
Pause for approval of the changed commitment
quiz.why: A recurring commitment changes the approved terms, even when its first charge is below the limit.

quiz.question: Which statement matches AP2 v0.2?
options: It is itself the bank or payment processor
Checkout and Payment Mandates provide linked authorization evidence
A free-text instruction replaces verification
quiz.why: The mandates provide verifiable authority. Payment credentials, processors and their checks still have roles.

quiz.question: A payment request times out. What does that prove?
options: It failed, so repeat the charge immediately
It succeeded, so mark the order paid
Neither; check the existing transaction outcome before retrying
quiz.why: An unknown response is not a known outcome. Reconcile the existing transaction and use a supported retry strategy to avoid duplicate charges.

quiz.question: The A2A task says completed. What else must the business check?
options: Nothing; completed proves payment and acceptance
Payment outcome and the agreed deliverable/acceptance criteria
Only whether the response sounded confident
quiz.why: Task status, payment status and customer acceptance are different facts.

quiz.question: Does using A2A require Google Cloud or a Google-only model?
options: Yes
No; it is an open protocol, with compatible implementations needed
Only if the service costs more than $50
quiz.why: A2A is open and supports agents built on different platforms. Interoperability still needs implementation and testing.
